name: IndependentChoices
summary: IndependentChoices is Arkansas Medicaid's self-directed option for adults who get personal care or ARChoices attendant care. Instead of agency care, the member gets a monthly cash allowance and hires their own personal assistant, who can be an adult child or other relative. Spouses, legal guardians, powers of attorney and income payees cannot be paid.
who_qualifies: Eligible for Arkansas Medicaid in a category that covers personal care, or SSI, or eligible for ARChoices.
Receiving, or medically eligible to receive, State Plan personal care or ARChoices attendant care.
Not living in a home owned, operated or controlled by a service provider, unless the provider is related by blood or marriage.

who_can_be_paid.adult_children_relatives: yes — family members other than those with legal responsibility may serve as personal assistants, including adult children.
who_can_be_paid.spouse: no — the state manual says a court-appointed legal guardian, spouse, power of attorney or income payee may not serve as a caregiver.
who_can_be_paid.parent_of_minor: no — IndependentChoices serves adults 18 and older.
who_can_be_paid.live_together: optional — the assistant may or may not live with the member.

pay.detail: There is no fixed family-caregiver wage. The monthly cash allowance is based on assessed hours and calculated at a maximum hourly rate of 78.11% of the Medicaid personal care rate; the member sets the assistant's wage within it. For ARChoices members, the allowance is also limited by the ARChoices service budget.

hours_or_budget: DHS staff or a DHS contractor use Task and Hour Standards to set hours. A support coordinator helps the member write a Cash Expenditure Plan showing how the allowance will be spent.

waitlist.detail: Through State Plan personal care there is no waitlist. Members coming through ARChoices need a waiver slot first, and ARChoices can have a waitlist.

self_directed_or_agency: The member (or a representative) is the employer of record. The financial management services agency, Public Partnerships LLC (PPL) since October 1, 2023, runs payroll and taxes.
how_to_apply: Apply for Medicaid long-term services and supports at Access Arkansas (access.arkansas.gov) or a local DHS county office.
Get a nurse assessment for personal care or ARChoices attendant care.
Ask to enroll in IndependentChoices; a counseling support coordinator and the fiscal agent help complete the enrollment packet.
Name a personal assistant and a backup caregiver; both pass background and registry checks before pay starts.

faqs.q: Can I get paid to take care of my mother in Arkansas?
faqs.a: Yes. If your mother qualifies for Medicaid personal care or ARChoices, she can enroll in IndependentChoices and hire you as her personal assistant.

faqs.q: Can a spouse be paid through IndependentChoices?
faqs.a: No. Arkansas rules say a spouse, court-appointed guardian, power of attorney or income payee cannot be the paid caregiver.
It is based on the hours DHS approves, at a maximum hourly rate of 78.11% of the Medicaid personal care rate.

faqs.q: Do I need a backup caregiver?
faqs.a: Yes. A backup plan naming a backup caregiver is required, and that person must also enroll.
Public Partnerships LLC (PPL) has been the financial management services vendor since October 1, 2023.

name: ARChoices in Homecare
summary: ARChoices in Homecare is an Arkansas Medicaid waiver that pays for home care for adults 65 and older and adults 21–64 with physical disabilities who would otherwise need a nursing home. Attendant care is given by agency workers, or the member can self-direct through IndependentChoices and hire a relative other than a spouse.
who_qualifies: Age 65 or older, or age 21–64 with a physical disability determined by Social Security or the DHS Medical Review Team.
Meets nursing home admission criteria at the intermediate level of care (people at the skilled level are not eligible).
Needs at least one ARChoices service.

who_can_be_paid.adult_children_relatives: limited — relatives such as adult children can be paid when the member self-directs attendant care through IndependentChoices.
who_can_be_paid.spouse: no — spouses and legal guardians cannot be hired as caregivers.
who_can_be_paid.parent_of_minor: no — ARChoices serves adults 21 and older.

pay.detail: No family-caregiver wage is published. In IndependentChoices, the monthly allowance is based on authorized hours at up to 78.11% of the Medicaid personal care rate and is limited by the member's ARChoices Individual Services Budget.

hours_or_budget: A DHS nurse assesses the member, and a person-centered service plan (PCSP) sets services and an Individual Services Budget. Services include attendant care, adult day, respite, home-delivered meals, emergency response systems, home modifications and prevocational services.

waitlist.detail: ARChoices is not an entitlement. Enrollment slots are limited (reported at about 11,500 a year) and a waiting list forms when they are full.

self_directed_or_agency: Either. Licensed agencies provide attendant care by default; members can self-direct through IndependentChoices, where they are the employer and PPL runs payroll.
how_to_apply: Apply at Access Arkansas (access.arkansas.gov) or call Access Arkansas at 855-372-1084, or visit a DHS county office.
Complete the financial review and a DHS nurse assessment for intermediate level of care.
Work with your case manager on a person-centered service plan.
If you want to pay a relative, choose IndependentChoices for attendant care.

faqs.a: Yes, through IndependentChoices. The member gets a cash allowance and can hire a relative such as an adult child. Spouses and guardians cannot be paid.
Adults 65 and older, or 21–64 with a physical disability, who need intermediate nursing-home-level care and meet Medicaid financial rules.
Often. ARChoices has a limited number of slots, and a waiting list forms when they fill.

faqs.q: What if I need skilled nursing-level care?
faqs.a: People determined to need the skilled level of care are not eligible for ARChoices.
Attendant care, adult day health, adult day services, case management, home modifications, home-delivered meals, emergency response systems, prevocational services and respite.
